questions.question: Farmer Ben has chickens and cows on his farm. He counts 18 heads and 50 legs altogether. How many chickens does he have?
questions.explanation:
Chickens have 2 legs, cows have 4 legs.
• Guess 1: 9 chickens, 9 cows → 9×2 + 9×4 = 18 + 36 = 54 legs (too many)
• Guess 2: 11 chickens, 7 cows → 11×2 + 7×4 = 22 + 28 = 50 legs ✓
Answer: 11 chickens

questions.question: In a pond, there are ducks and turtles. There are 14 animals altogether with 38 legs. How many turtles are there?
questions.explanation:
Ducks have 2 legs, turtles have 4 legs.
• Guess 1: 7 ducks, 7 turtles → 7×2 + 7×4 = 14 + 28 = 42 (too many)
• Guess 2: 9 ducks, 5 turtles → 9×2 + 5×4 = 18 + 20 = 38 ✓
Answer: 5 turtles

questions.question: Mia has 24 coins in her piggy bank. Some are 50¢ coins and some are 20¢ coins. The total value is $9.00. How many 50¢ coins does she have?
questions.explanation:
Work in cents. Total = 900¢.
• Guess 1: 12 fifty-cent, 12 twenty-cent → 12×50 + 12×20 = 600 + 240 = 840¢ (too low)
• Guess 2: 14 fifty-cent, 10 twenty-cent → 14×50 + 10×20 = 700 + 200 = 900¢ ✓
Answer: 14 fifty-cent coins

questions.question: A parking lot has cars and motorcycles. There are 22 vehicles with 72 wheels altogether. How many cars are there?
questions.explanation:
Cars have 4 wheels, motorcycles have 2 wheels.
• Guess 1: 13 cars, 9 motorcycles → 13×4 + 9×2 = 52 + 18 = 70 (too few)
• Guess 2: 14 cars, 8 motorcycles → 14×4 + 8×2 = 56 + 16 = 72 ✓
Answer: 14 cars

questions.question: In a quiz game, you earn 5 points for each correct answer and lose 1 point for each wrong answer. You answered 18 questions and scored 36 points. How many questions did you answer correctly?
questions.explanation:
Each correct = +5 pts, each wrong = −1 pt.
• Guess 1: 10 correct, 8 wrong → 10×5 − 8×1 = 50 − 8 = 42 (too high)
• Guess 2: 8 correct, 10 wrong → 8×5 − 10×1 = 40 − 10 = 30 (too low)
• Guess 3: 9 correct, 9 wrong → 9×5 − 9×1 = 45 − 9 = 36 ✓
Answer: 9 questions

questions.question: A garage has tricycles and bicycles. There are 28 vehicles with 74 wheels altogether. How many tricycles are there?
questions.explanation:
Tricycles have 3 wheels, bicycles have 2 wheels.
• Guess 1: 14 tricycles, 14 bicycles → 14×3 + 14×2 = 42 + 28 = 70 (too few)
• Guess 2: 16 tricycles, 12 bicycles → 16×3 + 12×2 = 48 + 24 = 72 (still too few)
• Guess 3: 18 tricycles, 10 bicycles → 18×3 + 10×2 = 54 + 20 = 74 ✓
Answer: 18 tricycles

questions.question: Ali bought 15 stamps. Some were 30¢ stamps and some were 50¢ stamps. He paid $5.50 altogether. How many 50¢ stamps did he buy?
questions.explanation:
Work in cents. Total = 550¢.
• Guess 1: 6 fifty-cent, 9 thirty-cent → 6×50 + 9×30 = 300 + 270 = 570¢ (too high)
• Guess 2: 4 fifty-cent, 11 thirty-cent → 4×50 + 11×30 = 200 + 330 = 530¢ (too low)
• Guess 3: 5 fifty-cent, 10 thirty-cent → 5×50 + 10×30 = 250 + 300 = 550¢ ✓
Answer: 5 fifty-cent stamps

questions.question: A workshop has 3-legged stools and 4-legged tables. There are 16 pieces of furniture with 55 legs altogether. How many stools are there?
questions.explanation:
Stools have 3 legs, tables have 4 legs.
• Guess 1: 8 stools, 8 tables → 8×3 + 8×4 = 24 + 32 = 56 (too many)
• Guess 2: 10 stools, 6 tables → 10×3 + 6×4 = 30 + 24 = 54 (too few)
• Guess 3: 9 stools, 7 tables → 9×3 + 7×4 = 27 + 28 = 55 ✓
Answer: 9 stools

questions.question: In a garden, there are spiders and beetles. Spiders have 8 legs and beetles have 6 legs. There are 12 creatures with 84 legs. How many spiders are there?
questions.explanation:
Spiders have 8 legs, beetles have 6 legs.
• Guess 1: 4 spiders, 8 beetles → 4×8 + 8×6 = 32 + 48 = 80 (too few)
• Guess 2: 7 spiders, 5 beetles → 7×8 + 5×6 = 56 + 30 = 86 (too many)
• Guess 3: 6 spiders, 6 beetles → 6×8 + 6×6 = 48 + 36 = 84 ✓
Answer: 6 spiders

questions.question: At a carnival, adult tickets cost $8 and child tickets cost $3. A group of 15 people paid $80 altogether. How many adults are in the group?
questions.explanation:
Adult ticket = $8, child ticket = $3.
• Guess 1: 5 adults, 10 children → 5×8 + 10×3 = 40 + 30 = $70 (too low)
• Guess 2: 8 adults, 7 children → 8×8 + 7×3 = 64 + 21 = $85 (too high)
• Guess 3: 7 adults, 8 children → 7×8 + 8×3 = 56 + 24 = $80 ✓
Answer: 7 adults
